newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore blue chips slide but other shares firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore blue chips slide but other shares firm.

text.p: Singapore's key share index fell on Wednesday as dealers continued to take profits from several key blue chip stocks.
But most shares were a little firmer and market sentiment appeared to suggest the index could rally again on Thursday.

"The market is getting more and more cautious as we move towards the Chinese New Year Holiday (February 7-8)," said one dealer. "But we might see something of a recovery. Liquidity is very high and foreign demand is relatively strong."
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed 10.78 points down at 2,240.01. Volume was a high 374.7 million shares.

Trading was dominated by new listing Chuan Soon Huat, which soared more than 75 percent from its initial public offer price of Singapore $0.35 on debut to reach a high of S$0.635. It closed at S$0.62 with more than 98 million shares traded.
The biggest loser of the day was auto retailer Cycle & Carriage, which dropped 50 cents to Singapore $16.40 after a newspaper reported it had cut prices for its Mercedes cars.
Dealers said the market could rise on Thursday and tipped gains for some electronics and banking stocks.
